title: 2D Vector Addition and Dot Product
spec: Write a module for 2D vector math. Implement `add_vectors(v1, v2)` where both arguments are tuples of two floats, unpacking them to compute their sum, and returning a new tuple. Implement `dot_product(v1, v2)` which similarly unpacks the tuples and returns the scalar dot product. Implement `scale_vector(v, factor)` which unpacks a single vector and multiplies both components by the factor. In the `main` block, define `v_a` as `(3.0, 4.0)` and `v_b` as `(1.0, 2.0)`. Call `add_vectors` with these variables, store the result in `sum_v`, and print `sum_v`. Then do the same for `dot_product`, storing and printing the scalar result.

title: Rectangle Area and Scaling
spec: Write a module for rectangle geometry. Implement `compute_area(width, height)` which returns the computed area. Implement `compute_perimeter(width, height)` which returns the perimeter. Implement `create_rectangle(width, height)` that simply returns the two arguments as a tuple. Implement `scale_rectangle(rect_tuple, factor)` which unpacks a `(width, height)` tuple, multiplies each dimension by the factor, and returns a new `(new_width, new_height)` tuple. In the driver block, define `width = 10` and `height = 20`. Pass them to `compute_area` and store the result. Then call `create_rectangle` to build a tuple `r = (10, 20)`, pass it to `scale_rectangle` with a factor of 2, store the resulting tuple in `scaled_rect`, and print it.

title: Time Interval Intersection
spec: Write a module to compute the intersection of 1D time intervals. Implement `intersect_intervals(i1, i2)`, where each interval is a tuple of a start and end time. Unpack them and use the built-in `max` and `min` functions to find the overlap; if the overlap is valid (start strictly less than end), return it as a tuple, else return None. Implement `merge_intervals(i1, i2)` which returns the bounding interval of both (minimum start, maximum end) as a tuple. Write a main block that defines `i_a = (10, 20)` and `i_b = (15, 25)`. Call the intersect function on them, store the result in a variable, and print it directly.

title: Key-Value Configuration Parsing
spec: Write a script that processes configuration lines. Implement `parse_line(line, fallback)` that splits a string by the equals sign (without passing a maxsplit argument). Unpack the split result into `key` and `value` on a single line, returning them as a tuple; if it fails due to unpacking an invalid number of items, catch the exception and return `(line, fallback)`. Implement `apply_setting(config_dict, pair_tuple)` which unpacks a `(key, value)` tuple and assigns it into the dictionary. Implement `get_setting(config_dict, key)` that returns the value. In the main function, initialize an empty dictionary, process the string `"port=8080"` passing `False` as the fallback, store the returned tuple, apply it to the dictionary, and print the dictionary.

title: List Pagination Helper
spec: Write a pagination module. Implement `get_bounds(page, page_size)` which calculates the zero-based start index and the limit, returning them as a tuple `(offset, limit)`. Implement `slice_items(items, bounds)` where `bounds` is that tuple; unpack it, compute the end index, and return the sliced list. Implement `get_total_pages(total_items, page_size)` which calculates the total pages using standard integer arithmetic. Finally, implement `create_page_response(items, total_pages)` which returns a dictionary with these two arguments mapped to string keys. In the driver code, generate a list of items, compute bounds for page 3 with size 10, storing it in `b_tuple`, pass it to `slice_items`, and print the result.

title: Text Normalization and Substitution
spec: Write a text normalization utility. Implement `normalize_spacing(text, max_iters)` which uses `text.replace("  ", " ")` repeatedly up to `max_iters` times to remove double spaces. Implement `create_pair(word1, word2)` which simply returns them as a tuple. Implement `apply_substitutions(text, subs)` where `subs` is a list of tuples. Iterate through it using `for old, new in subs:` and apply each substitution using the string `replace` method. In the main block, create an empty list named `subs`. Append the result of `create_pair("foo", "bar")` to it, then append `create_pair("baz", "qux")` on the next line. Call `apply_substitutions` on a test string with `subs` and print the result.

title: Undirected Graph Adjacency
spec: Write an undirected graph module using adjacency lists. Implement `add_edge(graph, edge_tuple)` where `edge_tuple` is a tuple of two node names. Unpack it and append each node to the other's list in the graph dictionary. Implement `check_adjacent(graph, edge_tuple)` which unpacks the tuple and returns True if the two nodes are directly connected in the graph. Include a driver that initializes an empty graph dictionary with empty lists for keys "A", "B", and "C". Define `edge1 = ("A", "B")`, pass it to `add_edge`, then do the same for `edge2 = ("B", "C")`. Finally, define a tuple for "A" and "C" and print the result of checking their adjacency.

title: File Path Splitting and Joining
spec: Write a file path utility. Import `os` and `sys` on the same line. Implement `split_path(path)` which calls `os.path.split(path)` to get the directory and filename, unpacks them on one line, then calls `os.path.splitext` on the filename to separate the name and extension, unpacks those, and returns a tuple of `(directory, extension)`. Implement `join_custom(dir_path, filename)` which safely joins the two arguments using `os.path.join`. Implement `get_fallback_ext(path, default_ext)` which calls `split_path`, ignores the directory, and returns a tuple of `(path, extension)` or `(path, default_ext)` if empty. Include a driver block that calls `join_custom` on `"/var/log"` and `"system.log"`, and prints the result.

title: Cartesian to Polar Conversions
spec: Write a module to convert between 2D coordinate systems. Import `math` and `cmath` on a single line. Implement `to_polar(x, y)` which uses `math.hypot(x, y)` for the radius and `math.atan2(y, x)` for the angle, returning them as a tuple. Implement `to_cartesian(r, theta)` which computes x and y using `math.cos` and `math.sin` multiplied by the radius, and returns `(x, y)`. Implement `distance(p1, p2)` where each is an `(x, y)` tuple; unpack them and use `math.hypot` to return the Euclidean distance. Write a main section that passes `3.0` and `4.0` into the polar function, stores the returned tuple in a variable `p_tuple`, and prints `p_tuple`.

title: Safe Dictionary Merging
spec: Write a dictionary utility script. Implement `merge_dicts(dict_a, dict_b)` that iterates over the key-value items of the second dictionary using a for loop, assigning each into the first dictionary, and returns the modified first dictionary. Implement `safe_get_list(target_dict, key)` which uses the dictionary `get(key, default)` method to return the existing list or an empty list if the key is not found. Implement `clone_dict(source_dict, default_val)` which iterates over the source dictionary and populates a new dictionary where all values are replaced by the default. In the driver, define `d1 = dict(a=1, b=2)` and on the next line `d2 = dict(c=3, d=4)`. Call `merge_dicts` with both dictionaries, store the result, and print it.

title: Linear Range Mapping
spec: Write a utility for linear value mapping. Implement `map_linear(value, range_pair)` where `range_pair` is a tuple containing two tuples: an input range and an output range. Unpack the pair into `in_range` and `out_range`. On subsequent lines, unpack `in_range` into min and max, and do the same for `out_range`. Compute the proportional ratio of the value within the input bounds, then apply it to the output range. Implement `clamp_value(value, limits)` which unpacks the limits tuple, computes the minimum of the value and the upper limit on one line, and then returns the maximum of the lower limit and that result on the next line. In main, create `in_r = (0, 10)` and `out_r = (0, 100)`. Combine them as `ranges = (in_r, out_r)`. Map the value 5 and print the result.

title: Complex Number Arithmetic
spec: Write a module for complex number arithmetic using tuples. Implement `add_complex(c1, c2)` where each argument is a `(real, imag)` tuple. Unpack both arguments on separate lines, compute their sum, and return a new tuple. Implement `multiply_complex(c1, c2)` which similarly unpacks both tuples on separate lines, computes the complex product (real*real - imag*imag for the real part, etc.), and returns it as a `(real, imag)` tuple. Implement `conjugate_complex(c)` which unpacks the single tuple and returns a new tuple with the imaginary part negated. In the driver block, define `c_a = (1.0, 2.0)` and `c_b = (3.0, 4.0)`. Call `multiply_complex` with them, store the result in a variable, and print it.

title: Matrix Dimensions and Transposition
spec: Write a matrix utility module. Implement `get_dimensions(matrix, default_cols)` which calculates the number of rows and columns, returning them as a tuple. Implement `create_empty(rows, cols)` which generates a 2D list of zeros using the given sizes. Implement `flatten_matrix(matrix, dims_tuple)` which unpacks the `(rows, cols)` tuple on one line and iterates through the matrix to return a single flat list. Implement `transpose_dimensions(dims_tuple)` which unpacks the dimensions and returns them reversed as a tuple. In the driver, call `create_empty(2, 3)`, store it, get its dimensions by calling `get_dimensions`, store that tuple, pass it to `transpose_dimensions`, and print the transposed tuple.

title: Rational Arithmetic
spec: Write a module with an entry function `calculate(operations)` that processes a list of mathematical operations on fractions. Each item in the input list is a tuple containing a string command and a pair tuple. The pair tuple contains two fraction tuples. Each fraction tuple contains two integers for numerator and denominator. Implement separate helper functions to handle addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division. Each helper must take exactly two fraction tuples and produce a new fraction tuple. Ensure every resulting fraction is reduced to its lowest terms by finding the greatest common divisor of its numerator and denominator. The entry function should return a list of the resulting fraction tuples. For example, passing the command add and a pair of one half and one third should return the tuple five sixths.

title: Line Segment Geometry
spec: Write a module with an entry function `analyze(segments)` that processes a list of line segments. Each segment is a tuple of two endpoints. Each endpoint is a tuple of two coordinates representing x and y. Create a helper function to compute the length of a segment using the standard distance formula, taking two endpoints as arguments. Create another helper function to compute the midpoint, which averages the x and y coordinates and returns a midpoint tuple. Create a third helper function to compute the slope of the segment as a float, returning a special string if the segment is vertical. The entry function should return a list of tuples containing the length and the midpoint tuple for each segment. For example, a segment from origin to three four will yield a tuple with length five and midpoint one point five two.

title: Box Intersection Detection
spec: Write an entry function `intersect(boxes)` that checks pairs of two dimensional bounding boxes for overlap. The input is a list of tuples, where each tuple contains two boxes to compare. Each box is defined by a tuple of its minimum corner point and maximum corner point. Both points are themselves tuples of x and y coordinates. Create a helper function that takes two one dimensional intervals, each represented as a minimum and maximum tuple, and returns true if they overlap. In the main function, first determine if the horizontal intervals intersect using the helper. Then, determine if the vertical intervals intersect using the helper. Return true if both evaluations are true. Iterate through the input pairs and return a list of boolean values. For example, if box A spans from origin to two two and box B spans from one one to three three, they overlap.

title: Spherical Distance Calculator
spec: Implement an entry function `distance(routes)` that calculates the great circle distance for a series of travel routes. The input is a list of routes, where each route is a tuple of two locations. Each location is a tuple of latitude and longitude in degrees. Create a helper function that takes a location tuple and converts both degrees to radians, returning a new tuple. Create another helper function that takes two radian location tuples and computes the central angle between them using the haversine formula. The entry function should convert the two locations, compute the central angle, and multiply it by the earth radius of six thousand three hundred seventy one kilometers. Return a list of the computed distances rounded to the nearest kilometer. For example, the distance between two points on the equator separated by one degree longitude is about one hundred eleven kilometers.

title: Cylinder Metrics
spec: Create an entry function `metrics(cylinders)` that computes the surface area and volume for a batch of cylinders. The input is a list of tuples, where each tuple contains the radius and height of a cylinder. Create a helper function that calculates the area of the circular base given the radius. Create a helper function that calculates the lateral surface area given the radius and height. Create a third helper function that calculates the total surface area by combining the results of the first two helpers. Create a fourth helper function that calculates the volume given the radius and height. The main function should iterate through the cylinders and return a list of tuples, each containing the total surface area and the volume rounded to two decimal places. For example, a cylinder with radius one and height two yields a surface area of eighteen point eight five and volume six point two eight.

title: Pendulum Period and Frequency
spec: Write a module with an entry function `oscillate(pendulums)` that calculates the period and frequency of various simple pendulums. The input is a list of tuples, where each tuple contains the length of the pendulum in meters and the local acceleration due to gravity. Create a helper function that calculates the period using the physical formula involving the square root of length divided by gravity, multiplied by two pi. Create another helper function that calculates the frequency as the reciprocal of the period. Both helpers should take the length and gravity as their two arguments. The entry function should apply these helpers and return a list of tuples containing the period and frequency, both rounded to three decimal places. For example, length two and gravity nine point eight yields a period of two point eight three eight and frequency zero point three five two.

title: Gas Law Scaler
spec: Provide an entry function `scale(states)` that evaluates changes in gas states using the ideal gas law. The input is a list of state changes, where each change is a tuple containing an initial state tuple and a multiplier tuple. The state tuple holds temperature and pressure. The multiplier tuple holds factors to scale the temperature and pressure respectively. Create a helper function that multiplies the initial state values by the multipliers to get the final state tuple. Create another helper function that calculates the ratio of the new volume to the old volume. Knowing volume is proportional to temperature divided by pressure, this helper should take the initial state tuple and final state tuple as its two arguments. The entry function should return a list of tuples containing the final state tuple and the volume ratio. For example, doubling temperature and halving pressure yields a final state with double values and a volume ratio of four.

title: Wave Properties Calculator
spec: Develop an entry function `waves(properties)` that calculates missing wave properties. The input is a list of tuples, each containing a wave speed and a frequency. Create a helper function that calculates the wavelength by dividing the speed by the frequency. Create another helper function that calculates the wave period by taking the reciprocal of the frequency. Create a third helper function that computes the angular frequency by multiplying the frequency by two pi. Each helper must accept the required parameters as individual arguments. The main function should process each input tuple using the helpers and return a list of tuples containing the wavelength and the angular frequency. For example, a speed of three hundred and frequency of fifty returns a tuple with wavelength six and angular frequency three hundred fourteen point one six.

title: Audio Signal Mixer
spec: Write an entry function `mix(signals)` that processes pairs of audio wave parameters. The input is a list of tuples, each containing two signal definitions. Each signal definition is a tuple of amplitude and frequency. Create a helper function that computes the combined maximum amplitude by adding the two individual amplitudes. Create another helper function that determines the beat frequency by calculating the absolute difference between the two frequencies. Both helpers should take the two signal definition tuples as arguments. The main function should iterate over the pairs and return a list of tuples containing the combined maximum amplitude and the beat frequency. For example, mixing a signal of amplitude two and frequency four hundred with a signal of amplitude three and frequency four hundred five yields a tuple of five and five.

title: Bounding Box Scaling
spec: Implement an entry function `resize(boxes)` that scales bounding boxes by a given factor. The input is a list of tuples, each containing a box tuple and a scale factor. A box tuple consists of its width and height. Create a helper function that multiplies both the width and height by the scale factor to return a new scaled box tuple. Create a helper function that calculates the area of a box tuple. Create a third helper function that calculates the perimeter of a box tuple. The main function should first scale each box, then use the other helpers to calculate the area and perimeter of the scaled box. Return a list of tuples containing the new area and the new perimeter. For example, scaling a box of width two and height three by a factor of two results in an area of twenty four and perimeter of twenty.

title: Circuit Impedance Calculator
spec: Write an entry function `impedance(components)` that calculates the total impedance for series electrical circuits. The input is a list of tuples, where each tuple contains the total resistance and total reactance of a circuit. Create a helper function to calculate the impedance magnitude by taking the square root of the sum of the squares of the resistance and reactance. Create another helper function to calculate the phase angle in radians by using the arctangent of the reactance divided by the resistance. Both helpers should take the resistance and reactance as two separate arguments. The main function should return a list of tuples containing the impedance magnitude and the phase angle rounded to four decimal places. For example, a resistance of three and reactance of four yields a magnitude of five and a phase angle of zero point nine two seven three.

title: Ellipse Geometry
spec: Create an entry function `measure(ellipses)` that calculates the area and eccentricity of ellipses. The input is a list of tuples, where each tuple contains the semi major axis and the semi minor axis of an ellipse. Create a helper function to calculate the area by multiplying pi by both axes. Create another helper function to calculate the focal distance by subtracting the square of the minor axis from the square of the major axis, then taking the square root. Create a third helper function that calculates the eccentricity by dividing the focal distance by the major axis. All helpers should accept the two axes as arguments. The main function should return a list of tuples containing the area and eccentricity rounded to three decimal places. For example, axes of five and three yield an area of forty seven point one two four and eccentricity of zero point eight.

title: Projectile Trajectory Range
spec: Develop an entry function `trajectory(launches)` that calculates the maximum height and horizontal range of projectiles. The input is a list of tuples, where each tuple contains the initial velocity in meters per second and the launch angle in radians. Create a helper function that computes the vertical velocity component given the initial velocity and angle. Create another helper function that computes the horizontal velocity component given the initial velocity and angle. Create a third helper function that calculates the maximum height using the vertical velocity and gravitational acceleration. The entry function should compute the total flight time using the vertical velocity, then calculate the horizontal range using the horizontal velocity and flight time. Return a list of tuples containing the maximum height and horizontal range rounded to two decimal places. For example, a velocity of ten and angle of zero point seven eight five radians yields a height of two point five five and range of ten point two.

title: Currency Exchange Arbitrage
spec: Write an entry function `trade(markets)` that evaluates currency exchange opportunities across two markets. The input is a list of tuples, each containing two exchange rates for a specific currency pair. The first rate is the buying price in market A, and the second rate is the selling price in market B. Create a helper function to calculate the potential profit margin by subtracting the buying price from the selling price. Create another helper function to determine the percentage yield by dividing the profit margin by the buying price and multiplying by one hundred. Both helpers should take the buying and selling prices as two arguments. The main function should return a list of tuples containing the profit margin and the percentage yield. For example, buying at one point two and selling at one point two six yields a margin of zero point zero six and a yield of five percent.

title: Gear Train Ratios
spec: Implement an entry function `gears(trains)` that calculates the speed and torque changes through pairs of gears. The input is a list of tuples, each containing the number of teeth on the driving gear and the number of teeth on the driven gear. Create a helper function to calculate the gear ratio by dividing the driven teeth by the driving teeth. Create a helper function that calculates the output speed by dividing an input speed by the gear ratio. This helper should take the input speed and gear ratio as its two arguments. Create a third helper function that calculates the output torque by multiplying an input torque by the gear ratio, taking these two as arguments. The main function should use an input speed of one thousand and input torque of ten for all calculations, and return a list of tuples containing the output speed and output torque. For example, ten driving teeth and twenty driven teeth yield an output speed of five hundred and output torque of twenty.

title: Image Crop Dimensions
spec: Write an entry function `crop(images)` that calculates the dimensions for cropping images to a square aspect ratio. The input is a list of tuples, each containing the original width and original height of an image. Create a helper function that determines the size of the square crop by finding the minimum of the width and height. Create another helper function that calculates the required offset by subtracting the crop size from a given dimension and dividing by two, rounding down. The main function should use the first helper to get the crop size. Then, it should use the second helper twice: once with the width and crop size to get the horizontal offset, and once with the height and crop size to get the vertical offset. Return a list of tuples containing the horizontal offset and the vertical offset. For example, a width of one hundred and height of eighty yields a crop size of eighty and an offset tuple of ten and zero.

title: Knight Move Validator
spec: Create an entry function `validate(moves)` that checks if a series of chess moves are valid for a knight. The input is a list of tuples, where each tuple contains a starting position and an ending position. Each position is a tuple of two integers representing the column and row on a chessboard from zero to seven. Create a helper function that calculates the absolute difference between two integer coordinates. In the main function, use the helper to find the difference in columns between the start and end positions. Use the helper again to find the difference in rows. A move is valid if the column difference is two and row difference is one, or if the column difference is one and row difference is two. Return a list of boolean values indicating if each move is valid. For example, moving from zero zero to one two is valid and returns true.

title: Grid Manhattan Distance
spec: Develop an entry function `navigate(paths)` that calculates distances between points on a standard grid. The input is a list of tuples, each containing a starting point and an ending point. Each point is a tuple of x and y integer coordinates. Create a helper function that calculates the absolute difference between two integer coordinates. The main function should use this helper twice for each pair of points: once to find the difference between the x coordinates, and once for the y coordinates. Create a helper function that computes the Manhattan distance by adding these two differences. Create a third helper function that computes the Chebyshev distance by finding the maximum of these two differences. Return a list of tuples containing the Manhattan distance and the Chebyshev distance. For example, moving from origin zero zero to three four yields a Manhattan distance of seven and Chebyshev distance of four.

title: Amortization Payment Calculator
spec: Write an entry function `finance(loans)` that calculates the monthly payment and total interest for a series of loans. The input is a list of tuples, each containing the principal amount and the annual interest rate as a decimal. Create a helper function to calculate the monthly payment using the standard amortization formula. The helper should divide the annual rate by twelve to get the monthly rate, assume a term of three hundred sixty months, and use the principal. Create another helper function to calculate the total interest paid. This helper should multiply the monthly payment by three hundred sixty and subtract the principal, taking the monthly payment and principal as its two arguments. Return a list of tuples containing the monthly payment and total interest rounded to two decimal places. For example, a principal of one hundred thousand and rate of zero point zero five yields a monthly payment of five hundred thirty six point eight two.

title: Color Luminance Contrast
spec: Implement an entry function `contrast(colors)` that evaluates the contrast ratio between pairs of grayscale colors. The input is a list of tuples, where each tuple contains two colors to compare. Each color is a float representing its relative luminance between zero and one. Create a helper function that returns the lighter luminance by taking the maximum of the two values. Create a helper function that returns the darker luminance by taking the minimum of the two values. Create a third helper function that calculates the contrast ratio. This helper should add zero point zero five to both the lighter and darker luminances, then divide the first sum by the second. The main function should return a list of the contrast ratios rounded to two decimal places. For example, comparing zero point eight and zero point two yields a ratio of three point four.

title: Triangle Properties
spec: Create an entry function `triangles(shapes)` that computes the area and perimeter of right angle triangles. The input is a list of tuples, where each tuple contains the base and the height of a right angle triangle. Create a helper function to calculate the hypotenuse using the Pythagorean theorem, taking the base and height as arguments. Create another helper function to calculate the area by multiplying the base by the height and dividing by two. Create a third helper function that calculates the perimeter by adding the base, height, and hypotenuse together. This helper should accept the base and height, call the hypotenuse helper, and return the sum of all three sides. The main function should return a list of tuples containing the area and perimeter. For example, a base of three and height of four yields an area of six and perimeter of twelve.

title: Classification Metrics
spec: Write an entry function `evaluate(matrices)` that calculates precision and recall for a set of confusion matrices. The input is a list of tuples, where each tuple contains two sub tuples. The first sub tuple contains true positives and false positives. The second sub tuple contains true negatives and false negatives. Create a helper function to calculate the precision by dividing true positives by the sum of true positives and false positives. Create a helper function to calculate the recall by dividing true positives by the sum of true positives and false negatives. Each helper should accept the necessary integer arguments directly. The main function should unpack the tuples, call the helpers, and return a list of tuples containing the precision and recall rounded to two decimal places. For example, a matrix with fifty true positives, ten false positives, and five false negatives yields a precision of zero point eight three and recall of zero point ninety one.

title: Stereo Panning Volumes
spec: Develop an entry function `pan(sounds)` that calculates the left and right channel volumes for stereo panning. The input is a list of tuples, each containing a base volume level and a pan position from negative one for full left to positive one for full right. Create a helper function to calculate the left multiplier by taking the square root of zero point five multiplied by one minus the pan position. Create a helper function to calculate the right multiplier by taking the square root of zero point five multiplied by one plus the pan position. Create a third helper function that multiplies the base volume by a given multiplier. The main function should use these helpers to compute the left and right volumes. Return a list of tuples containing the left volume and right volume rounded to two decimal places. For example, a volume of ten and pan of zero yields left and right volumes of seven point zero seven.

title: Text Column Alignment
spec: Implement an entry function `align(rows)` that formats a two column text table. The input is a list of tuples, where each tuple contains a left string and a right string. First, determine the maximum length of the left strings and the maximum length of the right strings by iterating over the rows. Create a helper function that takes a string and its target width, returning the string padded with spaces on the right to match the width. Create another helper function that takes a string and its target width, returning the string padded with spaces on the left. The entry function should iterate over the rows, use the helpers to pad the left and right strings with their respective maximum widths, and return a list of tuples containing the padded left and padded right strings. For example, a row of apple and ten aligned to widths of ten and five yields padded apple and padded ten.

title: Password Entropy and Strength
spec: Write an entry function `entropy(passwords)` that calculates the entropy and strength score of passwords. The input is a list of tuples, each containing a password string and the size of the character pool it was drawn from. Create a helper function to calculate the entropy in bits. This is done by multiplying the length of the password by the base two logarithm of the pool size. Create a helper function to determine the strength score. The score is a float computed by dividing the entropy by a baseline value of one hundred twenty eight bits, capping the result at one point zero. Both helpers should take the password and pool size as arguments where needed. Return a list of tuples containing the entropy and the strength score rounded to two decimal places. For example, an eight character password from a pool of sixty four characters yields an entropy of forty eight and a score of zero point three eight.

title: Quotient and Remainder Math
spec: Write a function `divide(pairs)` to perform basic math on pairs of numbers. Input is a list of tuples containing two integers. For each tuple, calculate the integer division quotient and remainder. Use a helper function for the division taking the two numbers that returns the quotient and remainder as a pair. Use another helper function taking the two numbers that calculates the greatest common divisor and the least common multiple, returning them as a pair. The main function must return two lists: a list containing the quotient and remainder pairs, and a list containing the divisor and multiple pairs. Return these two lists together as a final tuple pair. For example, given ten and three, the first list gets three and one, while the second list gets one and thirty.

title: Sensor Calibration Adjustments
spec: Write a function `calibrate(readings)` to adjust hardware measurements. Input is a list of raw voltage and raw temperature pairs. The task must compute calibrated values. Use a helper function taking the raw voltage and a scale factor of two, returning the scaled voltage and a boolean indicating if it is stable as a pair. Use another helper function taking the raw temperature and a fixed offset of five, returning the adjusted temperature and a boolean true as a pair. The main function iterates over the readings, applying the helpers. Collect the scaled voltage and adjusted temperature into a new pair. Return a list of these final calibrated voltage and temperature pairs.

title: Version Number Parsing
spec: Write a function `compare(versions)` to analyze software updates. Input is a list of string pairs representing an old version and a new version. Parse each string by splitting on the dot to get a major and minor number pair. Provide a helper that takes an old version string and a new version string, parses both, and returns a boolean pair indicating if the major version increased, and if the minor version increased. The main function iterates over the list of string pairs and returns a list of these boolean pairs. For example, given one dot zero and one dot two, return false and true.

title: Name Formatting Arrangement
spec: Write a function `arrange(names)` to standardize user profiles. Input is a list of strings containing a first name and a last name separated by a space. The task must create a list of formatted pairs. For each name, use a helper function that splits the string and returns a first name and last name string pair. Use a second helper taking the first and last strings that returns a pair where both are converted to uppercase. Use a third helper taking the first and last strings that returns a pair where the first is abbreviated to its initial and the last is capitalized. The main function collects the uppercase pair and the abbreviated pair, appending them sequentially. Return the final list of string pairs.

title: Server Load Balancing
spec: Write a function `balance(servers)` to shift traffic across infrastructure. Input is a list of server capacity and current load integer pairs. The task determines how much traffic to shift. A helper function takes the capacity and the load, returning the available headroom and a boolean indicating if the server is overloaded as a pair. Another helper takes the headroom and the overloaded boolean, returning a traffic shift amount and a string status code of either normal or critical as a pair. The main function iterates through the servers and applies these helpers. Return a list of these final shift amount and status code pairs.

title: Drone Motor Mixing
spec: Write a function `mix(commands)` to convert flight inputs into motor speeds. Input is a list of tuples containing throttle and steering. Throttle moves both left and right motors forward, while steering increases one and decreases the other. Use a helper function taking the throttle and steering that returns the unconstrained left speed and unconstrained right speed as a pair. Use another helper taking the left and right speeds that constrains each to be between zero and one hundred, returning the constrained left and right speeds as a pair. The main function maps these operations over the input. Return a list of these final left and right motor speed pairs.

title: Binary Search Tree Nodes
spec: Write a function `evaluate(elements)` to validate graph relationships. Input is a list of integer pairs representing a parent node and a child node. We want to check if the child is a valid left or right descendant. For each pair, use a helper function taking the parent and child that returns a boolean pair where the first element is true if the child is less than the parent, and the second is true if the child is greater than the parent. Provide another helper that takes the parent and child and returns their absolute difference and their sum as a pair. The main function must build a list of the boolean pairs and a list of the math pairs. Return both lists as a final tuple pair.

title: Robot Path Waypoints
spec: Write a function `waypoints(commands)` to simulate autonomous movement. Input is a list of distance and turn angle pairs. The task computes navigation waypoints. A helper function takes the current distance and a scale factor of ten, returning the scaled distance and a battery cost as a pair. Another helper takes the current turn angle and a fixed offset, returning the absolute angle and a string quadrant label as a pair. The main function steps through the commands, using these helpers to evaluate each movement step. Collect the scaled distance and absolute angle pairs into a result list. Return the list of these final waypoint pairs.

title: Sliding Window Bounds
spec: Write a function `window(limits)` to calculate viewing frames. Input is a list of center and radius pairs. The task computes the start and end bounds of a one dimensional viewing window for each pair. Use a helper function taking the center and radius that returns the start and end offsets as a pair. Another helper taking the start and end must check if the start is negative, shifting both start and end by the absolute value of the start, returning the updated pair. A third helper taking the shifted start and end ensures the end does not exceed one hundred, reducing both if necessary, returning the final clamped pair. Return a list of these final start and end pairs.

title: Date Span Shift
spec: Write a function `shift(spans)` to modify calendar bookings. Input is a list of month and day pairs. The task advances and rewinds the date by seven days, assuming all months have thirty days. A helper function takes the original month and day, adds seven days handling rollover to the next month, and returns the future month and day as a pair. Another helper takes the original month and day, subtracts seven days handling rollback to the previous month, and returns the past month and day as a pair. The main function loops through the inputs to create a list of past pairs and a list of future pairs. Return the list of past pairs and the list of future pairs as a single outer pair.

title: Stock High Low Tracking
spec: Write a function `track(prices)` to monitor asset volatility. Input is a list of current stock prices. The task must maintain a running lowest and highest price seen so far. A helper function takes a new price and the current low, returning the updated minimum and a boolean if it dropped as a pair. Another helper takes the new price and the current high, returning the updated maximum and a boolean if it peaked as a pair. The main function updates the running low and high for each price, and collects the updated minimum and maximum into a new pair at each step. Return a list of these minimum and maximum pairs.

title: Checkers Diagonal Moves
spec: Write a function `diagonals(pieces)` to generate board game logic. Input is a list of row and column pairs for pieces on a board. The task calculates possible diagonal move destinations. Use a helper function that takes the row and column and returns a list containing the forward left pair and the forward right pair. Use another helper that takes the row and column and returns a list containing the backward left pair and the backward right pair. A third helper takes a destination row and column, returning a boolean pair indicating if the row is within a zero to seven limit and if the column is within the limit. The main function applies these and returns a list of all valid destination pairs.

title: Recipe Ingredient Scaling
spec: Write a function `scale(ingredients)` to adjust cooking measurements. Input is a list of base quantity and portion multiplier pairs for a recipe. The task scales each ingredient up. A helper function takes the base quantity and the multiplier, returning the scaled quantity and a boolean indicating if it exceeds one hundred as a pair. Another helper takes the scaled quantity and the boolean, returning the final approved quantity and a string warning label as a pair. The main function iterates over the recipe inputs, applying the helpers sequentially. Return a list of these approved quantity and warning label pairs.

title: Dice Game Score
spec: Write a function `score(rolls)` to compute points in a tabletop game. Input is a list of dice roll pairs. The task computes a score for each pair based on matching values. A helper function takes the two dice and returns their base sum and a boolean indicating if they match as a pair. Another helper takes the sum and the matching boolean, returning the final multiplied score and a string classification of either double or normal as a pair. The main function collects these score and classification pairs into a list for each roll. Return the final list of score and classification pairs.

title: Pulley Belt Speeds
spec: Write a function `pulleys(diameters)` to evaluate mechanical systems. Input is a list of driver and driven pulley diameter pairs. The task calculates the speed ratio and output speed for each pair, assuming a constant input speed of one thousand. A helper function takes the driver and driven diameters and returns the mathematical ratio and the raw output speed as a pair. Another helper takes this ratio and output speed, returning a boolean pair indicating if the ratio is greater than one and if the speed is greater than five hundred. The main function iterates over the list and returns a list containing all the calculated boolean pairs.

title: Temperature Range Conversion
spec: Write a function `temperatures(celsius)` to translate weather data. Input is a list of minimum and maximum celsius pairs. We need to convert the endpoints to fahrenheit. A helper function takes a single celsius value and a string label, returning the converted fahrenheit value and the string label as a pair. The main function applies this helper to the minimum celsius with a low label, and to the maximum celsius with a high label. Another helper takes the minimum fahrenheit and maximum fahrenheit, returning the temperature difference and the average temperature as a pair. Return a list of these difference and average pairs.

title: Seismic Wave Amplitudes
spec: Write a function `seismic(waves)` to analyze geological events. Input is a list of primary wave and secondary wave amplitude pairs. The task calculates the intensity of each event. A helper function takes the primary and secondary amplitudes, subtracting the secondary from the primary, returning the difference and a boolean if it is positive as a pair. Another helper takes the difference and the positive boolean, returning an earthquake magnitude score and a string alert level as a pair. The main function loops through the events, leveraging the helpers to assess the severity. Return a list of these magnitude and alert pairs.

title: IP Address Subnet Masking
spec: Write a function `subnet(addresses)` to process network routing configurations. Input is a list of network address and subnet mask integer pairs. The task calculates the network identifier and the broadcast identifier. A helper function takes the address and the mask, applies a bitwise operation, and returns the network identifier and a boolean indicating if it is valid as a pair. Another helper takes the network identifier and the inverted mask, applies an operation to find the upper bound, and returns the broadcast identifier and a boolean as a pair. The main function processes all inputs and returns a list of these network and broadcast identifier pairs.

title: Character Frequency Counter
spec: Write a function `frequencies(text)` to build statistical models of language. Input is a single string. The task counts the occurrences of each character in the string. A helper function takes a dictionary of counts and a character, returning the old count and the updated count as a pair. After counting, extract all dictionary items into a list of character and count pairs. Use another helper taking the character and count that returns them swapped as a count and character pair. Sort this list to find the most frequent characters. Return the highest count and its character as a final pair.

title: Inventory Restock Levels
spec: Write a function `restock(inventory)` to manage warehouse supplies. Input is a list of current stock and minimum threshold pairs for various items. The task determines how many units to reorder. A helper function takes the current stock and the minimum threshold, returning the deficit amount and a boolean if it needs reordering as a pair. Another helper takes the deficit amount and a standard batch size of fifty, returning the required order quantity and the projected new stock level as a pair. The main function maps these calculations across the catalog. Return a list of these order quantity and new stock pairs.

title: Bipartite Graph Matching Checks
spec: Write a function `connect(nodes)` to validate edge assignments in a network. Input is a list of left node integers and a list of right node integers. The task generates connections between them. A helper function takes a left node and a right node, returning a pair of the two nodes if the left is strictly smaller than the right, or returning zeroes otherwise. Another helper takes the left node and right node, returning their product and their sum as a pair. The main function iterates over the two lists in parallel, building a list of valid node pairs and a list of math pairs. Return both lists inside a final tuple pair.

title: Battery Charge Cycles
spec: Write a function `cycles(logs)` to estimate hardware longevity. Input is a list of initial and final battery percentage pairs. The task computes the drain and the estimated degradation. A helper function takes the initial and final percentages, returning the drained amount and a boolean indicating if it was a deep discharge as a pair. Another helper takes the drain amount and the deep discharge boolean, returning an estimated degradation score and a severity level string as a pair. The main function processes the session logs sequentially. Return a list of the degradation score and severity pairs for all inputs.

title: Barcode Checksum Pairs
spec: Write a function `checksum(barcodes)` to validate scanned products. Input is a list of odd digit sum and even digit sum pairs from barcode scans. The task calculates a final check digit for each pair. A helper function takes the odd sum and a fixed multiplier of three, returning the multiplied result and a zero remainder as a pair. Another helper takes the multiplied odd result and the even sum, returning their combined total and the final check digit as a pair. The check digit is calculated as ten minus the modulo ten of the total. Return a list of the total and check digit pairs for each input.

title: Signal Peak Detection
spec: Write a function `peaks(samples)` to process audio waveforms. Input is a list of amplitude and time pairs. The task identifies points where the amplitude is greater than ten. A helper function takes an amplitude and time, returning a boolean true and the time if it is a peak, or false and zero if not, as a pair. Another helper takes two time values, returning the larger time and the smaller time as a pair. The main function filters the input using the first helper and collects the valid peak times. Return a list of the valid time and amplitude pairs that correspond to true peaks.

title: Currency Denomination Coins
spec: Write a function `coins(amounts)` to format financial transactions. Input is a list of integer amounts in cents. The task splits each amount into dollars and remaining cents. A helper function takes the total amount and a divisor of one hundred, returning the dollar count and the remainder as a pair. Another helper takes the dollar count and the remainder, returning a formatted dollar string and a formatted cents string as a pair. The main function loops over the amounts, applying the division and formatting helpers. Return a list of these formatted string pairs. For example, given one hundred twenty five, return a string of one and a string of twenty five.

title: Carpet and Room Measurements
spec: Write a function called `evaluate(dimensions)` that accepts a list of room measurements. Each measurement in the list is a pair containing the room length and the room width in feet. For each room, compute four distinct metrics. The first metric is the baseboard length, which is 2 times the length plus 2 times the width. The second metric is the floor area, which is the length multiplied by the width. The third metric is the expected cutting waste, calculated as the absolute difference between the length and the width, multiplied by a waste factor of 1.2. The fourth metric is the diagonal span across the room, which is the square root of the length squared plus the width squared. To keep the logic organized, write a dedicated helper function for each of the four metrics. Each helper function should accept the length and the width as separate arguments. Return a list of pairs where each input room produces two pairs in the final list: first append a pair containing the baseboard length and the floor area, and then append a pair containing the cutting waste and the diagonal span. For an input of 10 and 8, the output list should contain a pair of 36 and 80, followed by a pair of 2.4 and 12.8.

title: River Canoe Navigation
spec: Write a function called `navigate(speeds)` that accepts a list of paddle and current speeds. Each item in the list is a pair containing the boat paddle speed and the river current speed in miles per hour. Compute four distinct metrics for each pair. The first metric is the downstream speed, which is the paddle speed plus the current speed. The second metric is the upstream speed, calculated as the absolute difference between the paddle speed and the current speed. The third metric is the round trip time for a fixed distance of 12 miles, which is 12 divided by the downstream speed plus 12 divided by the upstream speed. The fourth metric is the efficiency ratio, defined as the paddle speed squared minus the current speed squared. To keep the logic organized, write a dedicated helper function for each of the four metrics. Each helper function should accept the two speeds as separate arguments. Return a list of pairs where each input pair produces two pairs in the final list: first append a pair containing the downstream and upstream speeds, and then append a pair containing the round trip time and the efficiency ratio. For an input of 5 and 3, the first appended pair is 8 and 2, and the second appended pair is 7.5 and 16.

title: Copper Wire Analysis
spec: Write a function called `analyze(wires)` that accepts a list of wire specifications. Each item in the list is a pair containing the wire diameter in millimeters and the wire length in meters. Compute four metrics for each wire. The first metric is the cross sectional area, which is 3.14 times the diameter squared divided by 4. The second metric is the electrical resistance, calculated as the length divided by the area, multiplied by a resistivity factor of 0.017. The third metric is the total volume of the metal, which is the area multiplied by the length. The fourth metric is the outer surface area, calculated as 3.14 times the diameter times the length. To keep the logic organized, write a dedicated helper function for each of the four metrics. Each helper function should accept the diameter and the length as separate arguments. Return a list of pairs where each input wire produces two pairs in the final result: first append a pair of the area and resistance, and then append a pair of the volume and surface area. For an input of 2 and 10, the first pair is 3.14 and 0.054, and the second pair is 31.4 and 62.8.

title: Sunlight Shadow Casting
spec: Write a function called `sunlight(measurements)` that takes a list of outdoor measurements. Each measurement is a pair containing an object height and its shadow length in meters. Compute four metrics for each pair. The first metric is the hypotenuse distance from the top of the object to the tip of the shadow, using the square root of the sum of the squares. The second metric is the sun tangent ratio, which is the height divided by the shadow length. The third metric is the area of the shadow triangle, calculated as the height times the shadow length divided by 2. The fourth metric is the perimeter of the shadow triangle, which is the height plus the shadow length plus the hypotenuse. To keep the logic organized, write a dedicated helper function for each of the four metrics. Each helper function should accept the height and the shadow length as separate arguments. Return a list of pairs where each input produces two pairs in the final list: first append a pair containing the hypotenuse and the tangent ratio, and then append a pair containing the area and the perimeter. For an input of 3 and 4, the first pair should be 5 and 0.75, and the second pair should be 6 and 12.

title: Simple Machine Forces
spec: Write a function called `leverage(forces)` that takes a list of force measurements. Each item is a pair containing an effort force and a load force in newtons. Compute four metrics for each pair. The first metric is the mechanical advantage, which is the load force divided by the effort force. The second metric is the total force exerted on the system, which is the load force plus the effort force. The third metric is the net force difference, calculated as the absolute difference between the load force and the effort force. The fourth metric is the total work proxy over a distance of 10 meters, which is the sum of the forces multiplied by 10. To keep the logic organized, write a dedicated helper function for each of the four metrics. Each helper function should accept the effort force and the load force as separate arguments. Return a list of pairs where each input produces two pairs: first append a pair of the mechanical advantage and the total force, and then append a pair of the net force difference and the total work proxy. For an input of 50 and 200, the first pair is 4 and 250, and the second pair is 150 and 2500.

title: Alpine Ski Slope Ratings
spec: Write a function called `evaluate(slopes)` that accepts a list of mountain slope dimensions. Each item is a pair containing the vertical drop and the horizontal run in meters. Compute four metrics for each slope. The first metric is the straight line slope distance, which is the square root of the drop squared plus the run squared. The second metric is the gradient percentage, which is the drop divided by the run, multiplied by 100. The third metric is the glide speed estimate, calculated as the square root of 19.6 times the drop. The fourth metric is the safety rating, which is the run squared divided by the drop. To keep the logic organized, write a dedicated helper function for each of the four metrics. Each helper function should accept the vertical drop and horizontal run as separate arguments. Return a list of pairs where each input produces two pairs: first append a pair containing the slope distance and the gradient percentage, and then append a pair containing the glide speed and the safety rating. For an input of 30 and 40, the first pair is 50 and 75, and the second pair is 24.2 and 53.3.

title: Optical Lens Properties
spec: Write a function called `optics(lenses)` that takes a list of lens configurations. Each configuration is a pair containing the object distance and the focal length in centimeters. Compute four metrics for each configuration. The first metric is the image distance, which is the object distance times the focal length, divided by the difference of the object distance and the focal length. The second metric is the magnification ratio, which is the focal length divided by the difference of the object distance and the focal length. The third metric is the optical power proxy, calculated as 100 divided by the focal length plus 100 divided by the object distance. The fourth metric is the total system span, which is the object distance plus the absolute value of the computed image distance. To keep the logic organized, write a dedicated helper function for each of the four metrics. Each helper function should accept the object distance and the focal length as separate arguments. Return a list of pairs where each input produces two pairs: first append a pair of the image distance and the magnification, and then append a pair of the optical power and the system span. For an input of 30 and 10, the first pair is 15 and 0.5, and the second pair is 13.3 and 45.

title: Electronic Capacitor Energy
spec: Write a function called `circuit(components)` that takes a list of capacitor specifications. Each item is a pair containing the capacitance in microfarads and the applied voltage in volts. Compute four metrics for each capacitor. The first metric is the stored charge, which is the capacitance multiplied by the voltage. The second metric is the stored energy, calculated as 0.5 times the capacitance times the voltage squared. The third metric is the displacement current over one millisecond, which is the stored charge divided by 0.001. The fourth metric is the force between plates proxy, which is the capacitance squared times the voltage squared divided by 2. To keep the logic organized, write a dedicated helper function for each of the four metrics. Each helper function should accept the capacitance and the voltage as separate arguments. Return a list of pairs where each input produces two pairs: first append a pair of the charge and the energy, and then append a pair of the displacement current and the plate force proxy. For an input of 10 and 5, the first pair is 50 and 125, and the second pair is 50000 and 1250.

title: Solar Panel Yield
spec: Write a function called `solar(panels)` that takes a list of solar panel readings. Each item is a pair containing the panel area in square meters and the solar irradiance in watts per square meter. Compute four metrics for each panel. The first metric is the ideal power, which is the area multiplied by the irradiance. The second metric is the usable power, calculated as the ideal power multiplied by an efficiency factor of 0.2. The third metric is the thermal loss, which is the ideal power multiplied by 0.8. The fourth metric is the estimated voltage, calculated as the square root of the usable power multiplied by a base resistance of 10. To keep the logic organized, write a dedicated helper function for each of the four metrics. Each helper function should accept the area and the irradiance as separate arguments. Return a list of pairs where each input produces two pairs: first append a pair containing the ideal power and the usable power, and then append a pair containing the thermal loss and the estimated voltage. For an input of 2 and 500, the first pair is 1000 and 200, and the second pair is 800 and 44.7.

title: Acoustic Doppler Shift
spec: Write a function called `acoustic(velocities)` that takes a list of movement speeds. Each item is a pair containing an approaching source velocity and an observer velocity in meters per second. Compute four metrics for each situation. The first metric is the frequency multiplier, which is 340 plus the observer velocity, all divided by 340 minus the source velocity. The second metric is the closing speed, which is the source velocity plus the observer velocity. The third metric is the wavelength compression factor, calculated as 1 minus the source velocity divided by 340. The fourth metric is the echo return time for a 10000 meter gap, which is 20000 divided by the closing speed. To keep the logic organized, write a dedicated helper function for each of the four metrics. Each helper function should accept the source velocity and the observer velocity as separate arguments. Return a list of pairs where each input produces two pairs: first append a pair of the frequency multiplier and the closing speed, and then append a pair of the compression factor and the echo time. For an input of 40 and 10, the first pair is 1.16 and 50, and the second pair is 0.88 and 400.

title: Highway Traffic Density
spec: Write a function called `traffic(segments)` that accepts a list of road section data. Each item is a pair containing the number of vehicles and the road segment length in kilometers. Compute four metrics for each section. The first metric is the vehicle density, which is the number of vehicles divided by the road length. The second metric is the average spacing between vehicles in meters, calculated as the length divided by the vehicles, multiplied by 1000. The third metric is the capacity flow, which is the vehicle density multiplied by a speed limit of 80. The fourth metric is the congestion index, which is the square of the vehicles divided by the length. To keep the logic organized, write a dedicated helper function for each of the four metrics. Each helper function should accept the number of vehicles and the segment length as separate arguments. Return a list of pairs where each input produces two pairs: first append a pair of the vehicle density and the average spacing, and then append a pair of the capacity flow and the congestion index. For an input of 200 and 5, the first pair is 40 and 25, and the second pair is 3200 and 8000.

title: Mechanical Spring Oscillation
spec: Write a function called `oscillation(springs)` that accepts a list of physical spring systems. Each system is a pair containing the spring constant in newtons per meter and the attached mass in kilograms. Compute four metrics for each system. The first metric is the angular frequency squared, which is the spring constant divided by the mass. The second metric is the oscillation period proxy, calculated as 6.28 divided by the square root of the angular frequency squared. The third metric is the maximum kinetic energy for a 10 centimeter displacement, which is 0.5 times the spring constant times 0.01. The fourth metric is the peak force at 10 centimeters, which is the spring constant times 0.1 plus the mass times 9.8. To keep the logic organized, write a dedicated helper function for each of the four metrics. Each helper function should accept the spring constant and the mass as separate arguments. Return a list of pairs where each input produces two pairs: first append a pair containing the angular frequency squared and the period proxy, and then append a pair containing the kinetic energy and the peak force. For an input of 400 and 4, the first pair is 100 and 0.628, and the second pair is 2 and 79.2.

title: Typography Layout Scaling
spec: Write a function called `typography(fonts)` that takes a list of font configurations. Each configuration is a pair containing the font size in points and the screen resolution in dots per inch. Compute four metrics for each configuration. The first metric is the physical size in inches, which is the font size divided by 72. The second metric is the size in pixels, calculated as the size in inches multiplied by the screen resolution. The third metric is the line height in pixels, which is the size in pixels multiplied by 1.5. The fourth metric is the estimated character width in pixels, calculated as the size in pixels multiplied by 0.6. To keep the logic organized, write a dedicated helper function for each of the four metrics. Each helper function should accept the font size and the screen resolution as separate arguments. Return a list of pairs where each input produces two pairs: first append a pair of the size in inches and the size in pixels, and then append a pair of the line height and the character width. For an input of 36 and 96, the first pair is 0.5 and 48, and the second pair is 72 and 28.8.

title: Material Thermal Expansion
spec: Write a function called `thermal(materials)` that takes a list of heating scenarios. Each scenario is a pair containing the original material length in meters and the temperature change in degrees celsius. Compute four metrics for each scenario. The first metric is the length expansion, which is the original length times the temperature change times a coefficient of 0.0001. The second metric is the new final length, which is the original length plus the expansion. The third metric is the thermal strain percentage, calculated as the expansion divided by the original length multiplied by 100. The fourth metric is the structural stress if confined, which is the expansion divided by the original length multiplied by an elastic modulus of 200000. To keep the logic organized, write a dedicated helper function for each of the four metrics. Each helper function should accept the original length and the temperature change as separate arguments. Return a list of pairs where each input produces two pairs: first append a pair containing the expansion and the final length, and then append a pair containing the strain percentage and the confined stress. For an input of 10 and 50, the first pair is 0.05 and 10.05, and the second pair is 0.5 and 1000.

title: Satellite Orbit Characteristics
spec: Write a function called `orbit(satellites)` that takes a list of space objects. Each object is a pair containing the orbital radius in kilometers and the central body mass proxy. Compute four metrics for each object. The first metric is the orbital velocity squared, which is the mass proxy divided by the radius. The second metric is the orbital period proxy, calculated as 6.28 times the radius divided by the square root of the velocity squared. The third metric is the kinetic energy proxy, which is 0.5 times a standard satellite mass of 1000 times the velocity squared. The fourth metric is the escape velocity squared, which is 2 times the orbital velocity squared. To keep the logic organized, write a dedicated helper function for each of the four metrics. Each helper function should accept the orbital radius and the mass proxy as separate arguments. Return a list of pairs where each input produces two pairs: first append a pair of the orbital velocity squared and the period proxy, and then append a pair of the kinetic energy proxy and the escape velocity squared. For an input of 400 and 16000000, the first pair is 40000 and 12.56, and the second pair is 20000000 and 80000.

title: Arterial Blood Pressure
spec: Write a function called `pressure(patients)` that takes a list of blood pressure readings. Each reading is a pair containing the systolic pressure and the diastolic pressure. Compute four metrics for each reading. The first metric is the pulse pressure, which is the systolic pressure minus the diastolic pressure. The second metric is the mean arterial pressure, calculated as the diastolic pressure plus one third of the pulse pressure. The third metric is the stroke work index, which is the pulse pressure multiplied by a constant factor of 1.2. The fourth metric is the wall stress proxy, calculated as the systolic pressure multiplied by the diastolic pressure, all divided by 100. To keep the logic organized, write a dedicated helper function for each of the four metrics. Each helper function should accept the systolic and the diastolic pressure as separate arguments. Return a list of pairs where each input produces two pairs: first append a pair containing the pulse pressure and the mean arterial pressure, and then append a pair containing the stroke work index and the wall stress proxy. For an input of 120 and 80, the first pair is 40 and 93.3, and the second pair is 48 and 96.

title: Tennis Court Dimensions
spec: Write a function called `tennis(courts)` that takes a list of court measurements. Each measurement is a pair containing the full court length and the full court width in feet. Compute four metrics for each court. The first metric is the total playing area, which is the length multiplied by the width. The second metric is the singles playing area, calculated as the length multiplied by the width minus 9. The third metric is the area of a single service box, which is half of the length multiplied by half of the singles width. The fourth metric is the boundary tape length, calculated as 2 times the length plus 2 times the width. To keep the logic organized, write a dedicated helper function for each of the four metrics. Each helper function should accept the court length and width as separate arguments. Return a list of pairs where each input produces two pairs: first append a pair of the total area and the singles area, and then append a pair of the service box area and the boundary tape length. For an input of 78 and 36, the first pair is 2808 and 2106, and the second pair is 526.5 and 228.

title: Acoustic Wavelengths
spec: Write a function called `acoustics(sounds)` that takes a list of audio tones. Each tone is a pair containing the frequency in hertz and the medium speed of sound in meters per second. Compute four metrics for each tone. The first metric is the full wavelength, which is the speed of sound divided by the frequency. The second metric is the half wavelength, which is the full wavelength divided by 2. The third metric is the quarter wave pipe length, calculated as the full wavelength divided by 4. The fourth metric is the beat frequency with a reference tone of 440 hertz, which is the absolute difference between the frequency and 440. To keep the logic organized, write a dedicated helper function for each of the four metrics. Each helper function should accept the frequency and the speed of sound as separate arguments. Return a list of pairs where each input produces two pairs: first append a pair containing the full wavelength and the half wavelength, and then append a pair containing the pipe length and the beat frequency. For an input of 340 and 340, the first pair is 1 and 0.5, and the second pair is 0.25 and 100.

title: Photographic Exposure Values
